Today most are launched fire-and-forget from `_initBabylon` and the scene renders procedural fallbacks (cone+sphere units, box+roof houses, cone trees) that morph into the real assets as their promises resolve. Players see a visibly upgrading scene for the first 2–5 seconds. We want a loading screen that: - Blocks the scene reveal until every asset needed for a full-quality first frame is ready. - Shows a progress bar tracking that load. - Fades the scene in once everything is ready. Scope is 3D only. The 2D legacy renderer loads only `tilemap.png` and is fast enough to keep its current immediate-reveal behavior. ## Approach Add a `whenReady(): Promise` API + `onProgress(loaded, total, label?)` callback on `Renderer3D`. Convert the existing fire-and-forget loads into a tracked bundle. `main.js` shows a loading overlay between the setup-screen → game-screen swap and the first reveal, ticks the progress bar from the renderer's events, and fades the canvas in once the promise resolves. ### 1. Renderer-side: tracked asset bundle In `src/renderer-3d.js`, replace the fire-and-forget pattern in `_initBabylon` (lines ~3686–3702) with an explicit `_assetBundle` — an array of `{ id, label, promise }` items collected during init: ``` this._assetBundle = [ { id: 'babylon', label: 'engine', promise: _ensureBabylonReady() }, { id: 'atlas', label: 'sprites', promise: loadImagesP() }, { id: 'house', label: 'houses', promise: _loadHouseModel() }, { id: 'paladin', label: 'paladin', promise: _loadPaladinModel() }, { id: 'trees', label: 'forest', promise: _loadTreePackManifest() }, ]; ``` Walking / idle animation GLBs are nested inside `_loadPaladinModel` — that loader already awaits them when present, so wrapping it is enough. Expose `renderer.whenReady()` returning `Promise.all(this._assetBundle.map(b => b.promise))` (mapped to `void`). Expose `renderer.onProgress = (loaded, total, label) => {...}` — fired synchronously each time a bundle item resolves (regardless of order). Each bundle item's `.then(...).finally(() => this._emitProgress(id))` hook keeps the count moving even on individual fallback paths. `loadImages()` (`src/renderer.js:290` for 2D, mirrored on 3D) currently uses a callback. Add a thin internal helper that returns the same promise so it slots into the bundle without changing 2D behavior. ### 2. HTML overlay In `index.html`, add a sibling inside `#game-screen`, sitting above `#canvas-wrapper`: ```html

``` Match the existing dark gothic theme (uses the same CSS custom properties on `:root` that the setup card uses). One file, ~10 lines. ### 3. Extract a helper `_showLoadingAndReveal(renderer)`: ``` const overlay = document.getElementById('loading-overlay'); const fill = overlay.querySelector('.loading-bar-fill'); const label = overlay.querySelector('.loading-label'); const canvas = document.getElementById('game-canvas'); overlay.hidden = false; canvas.classList.remove('canvas-ready'); fill.style.width = '0%'; renderer.onProgress = (loaded, total, what) => { fill.style.width = `${Math.round(100 * loaded / total)}%`; if (what) label.textContent = `Loading ${what}…`; }; await renderer.whenReady(); // One extra animation frame so the first draw runs while overlay is still up. renderer.draw(); await new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(r)); canvas.classList.add('canvas-ready'); // 400 ms fade in overlay.classList.add('fading-out'); // 300 ms fade out setTimeout(() => { overlay.hidden = true; overlay.classList.remove('fading-out'); }, 350); ``` Replace the synchronous `redraw()` (line 303) and any other "first draw" sites with `await _showLoadingAndReveal(renderer)`.
